name: Bind the Linux Canvas canary click check to a post-dispatch frame

bounded_outcome: Make the isolated Linux expected-abort Canvas canary associate its initial pre-Tab path-focus click with exactly one raw primary press/release observed in egui frames strictly after watermark W, and require the paired field state to belong to that exact click-event frame. Keep the later R3.5 stationary recovery click as a separate action with its own evidence and no pointer movement. Report observed frame ordering only; do not infer OS-to-egui wall-clock latency or its cause. Preserve the full R3.5 focus-transition, recovery, expected-abort, clipboard, and byte-preservation acceptance.

confirmed_sampling_gap.observation: The post-click wait can accept a paired field observation recorded during pointer positioning, before click dispatch, because its predicate is bounded by an earlier geometry watermark and does not require a post-dispatch target click. A later clicked=true guard then fails closed. The trace records the click in a later frame but cannot explain the OS-to-egui timing delay.
confirmed_sampling_gap.source_review: Two independent static reviews support the sampling gap; a follow-up review specified exact-frame pairing and no retry after ambiguous post-dispatch input.
confirmed_sampling_gap.cause_limit: Do not claim why the OS-to-egui event appears later; logs prove only the event timing observed by the harness and egui.

eframe_app_ron_paths.macos_path_basis: HOME is appDataContainer/home; pinned eframe preserves the OpenObsidian app ID spelling in its macOS Application Support storage path.
eframe_app_ron_paths.macos_directory_setup: Pre-create the exact OpenObsidian spelling requested by eframe so case-insensitive runner volumes do not preserve a conflicting lowercase directory entry.

Every allowed change must still be phase-authorized and its resulting bytes must pass the existing eframe state and path-leakage checks.

pointer_positioning_coalescing_evidence.acceptance: Continue accepting an ordered subsequence of the two planned destinations when the backend coalesces movement, while requiring the target move and rejecting duplicates or other positions.
pointer_positioning_coalescing_evidence.meaning: The evidence reports a neutral move coalesced when destination index 0 is absent from the observed ordered sequence; this does not make the neutral move mandatory.

scope: After geometry and refresh guards pass, capture the latest fresh same-frame path/ID pair immediately before dispatch. Require stable distinct response IDs, known idle receiver states, released primary button, and no primary-button event since the prePositionFrame state boundary.

Define prePositionFrame from the frame_nr shared by beforeClickFieldPair path/ID rows and exactly one complete trace record, captured immediately before xdotool windowfocus. Treat its trace as the pre-command state/event boundary: preserve its raw event vector as evidence, but do not attribute those events to the subsequent focus or pointer commands because they may have occurred earlier in that frame. Require the primary button released and all five current modifier bits clear at this boundary. Record the focus command start/end lines and successful completion, then verify the intended X11 window is focused before any pointer movement. Between prePositionFrame and positioningStartFrame, permit no raw event except an optional WindowFocused(true) attributed to that command within this bounded frame interval and optional ModifiersChanged(NONE). The focus event may be logged after the xdotool command returns because egui event delivery is asynchronous; associate it by frame interval, command record, and confirmed target-window focus rather than requiring its log line to fall inside the command's wall-clock interval. Require an event-free, unique complete paired path/ID trace frame after windowfocus returns and before pointer movement, and name it positioningStartFrame. Define W as the frame_nr shared by the immediately-before-dispatch path/ID rows; set clickDispatchWatermark to their maximum log line plus W and keep the earlier geometry baseline for geometry and pre-dispatch retry purposes only. Require exactly one complete focus-trace record for W, stable enabled distinct response IDs/rectangles/scale, pointer at the intended path point, primary button up, and all five current modifier bits clear at W.

Extend only the canary-gated frame trace to record every raw event in vector order for each frame, including frame_nr, per-frame event_index, and a safe event-kind tag. For PointerButton, record button, pressed state, logical position, and all five modifier bits (alt/ctrl/shift/mac_cmd/command); for PointerMoved, record logical position; for WindowFocused, record focused state; for ModifiersChanged, record all five bits. Also record the five current modifier bits and primary-button-down state on every trace frame. Never log text, paste, IME, or clipboard contents. Correlate trace and field rows by frame_nr because Rust emits the trace before the paired field diagnostics.

Require complete, unique, consecutive trace records from prePositionFrame through W. Treat prePositionFrame only as the state/event boundary described above; preserve its raw event vector but do not apply the subsequent-command allowlist to it. From the next frame through positioningStartFrame, allow only the optional WindowFocused(true) attributed to the recorded xdotool windowfocus command within the bounded frame interval and optional ModifiersChanged(NONE); require positioningStartFrame itself to be event-free. From positioningStartFrame through W, allow only PointerMoved events attributable in order to the two logged xdotool mousemove destinations, plus optional ModifiersChanged(NONE). Map the xdotool window-local pixel destinations (5,5) and (clickX,clickY) into egui logical points using the stable pixels-per-point scale. Accept an ordered subsequence of those two destinations to account for backend coalescing, but require the target destination (clickX,clickY) to be observed; every observed PointerMoved position must match the next allowed destination per axis within 1.5 physical pixels: abs(dx) * pixelsPerPoint <= 1.5 and abs(dy) * pixelsPerPoint <= 1.5 (equivalently 1.5 / pixelsPerPoint logical points per axis), and no duplicate or other move is allowed. Record command boundaries and coordinates. Require the paired W pointer to match the target destination. Position movement may arrive in W, but no PointerMoved event is allowed after W. Reject primary/secondary buttons, keys/text/paste/IME, wheel/touch, other focus events, and unknown events throughout these pre-dispatch intervals. Immediately before dispatch, require W to show no primary-button event, the primary button released, and all five current modifier bits clear. Retain pre-dispatch retry behavior only for failures detected before click dispatch.

After capturing and validating the watermark, send exactly one coordinate click synchronously: perform no await, delay, screenshot, log wait, pointer action, or other input between watermark capture and click dispatch. If unexpected raw input is observed in that interval, fail before text entry.

The R3.6-instrumented click is the initial path-field focus click: its two scripted pointer-positioning commands precede it, and it establishes the event-free pre-Tab baseline before the existing Tab-induced focus loss and recovery. The R3.5 recovery sequence later sends a separate stationary target click at the already positioned pointer, after the two stable recovery observations and before ArrowRight. That later click retains its existing fresh clicked/geometry/pointer guards and sends no pointer movement. Report separate counters: target_coordinate_click_dispatch_attempts counts only the initial traced click and must equal one; stationary_recovery_click_dispatch_attempts counts only the later recovery click and must equal one. The W+1-through-initial-click exact raw press/release contract applies only to the first click; do not conflate the two click phases.

From W+1 through the click frame, require exactly one complete trace record for every consecutive frame, with no missing or duplicate frame records, and preserve every frame’s raw event vector order. Accept exactly one primary press followed by exactly one primary release, both with all five event modifier bits clear, plus zero or more ModifiersChanged(NONE) events; reject any nonempty modifier change, pointer move, key/text/paste/IME event, other button, wheel/touch event, window-focus change, other/unknown event, or incomplete trace. Require all five current modifier bits clear at W and after release. Preserve event_index when events share a frame.

Require press.frame_nr > W. Treat this as observed egui frame ordering for the single initial pre-Tab focus click, not a measurement of dispatch-to-egui wall-clock latency. Compare each event position directly with the path and ID response rectangles in the same egui logical-point coordinate space; require both positions inside the path rectangle and outside the sibling ID rectangle. Also require the press and release positions to match each other and the paired W pointer per axis within 1.5 physical pixels: abs(dx) * pixelsPerPoint <= 1.5 and abs(dy) * pixelsPerPoint <= 1.5 (equivalently 1.5 / pixelsPerPoint logical points per axis), with stable geometry, scale, and distinct response IDs. If press and release share a frame, require press.event_index < release.event_index; otherwise require press.frame_nr < release.frame_nr. The raw release, path Response::clicked=true observation, accepted path widget row, and accepted sibling widget row must all have the same initial-click frame_nr. The later stationary recovery click is a distinct R3.5 action and does not enter this initial-click frame comparison.

Require the target click observation line to be newer than clickDispatchWatermark.line as a secondary check, no sibling click, and the primary button released after the click. Use strict frame_nr comparisons for frame freshness; log-line order alone never proves a post-dispatch event.

A Response::clicked=true observation alone is insufficient proof of one raw click. Fail closed on missing, duplicate, reordered, modified, unrelated, out-of-geometry, sibling, or unpaired raw events or mismatched frame relations.

After dispatch, timeout, duplicate/ambiguous raw button events, sibling click, stale/mismatched pair, or missing exact-frame evidence aborts before text entry. Do not retry another click after a dispatch whose outcome is ambiguous.

Keep existing retries only for failures detected before click dispatch; leave ordinary Linux field entry, macOS/Windows input paths, production UI behavior, Rust semantics, and unrelated workflow acceptance unchanged.
out_of_scope: Weakening any target, sibling, focus, receiver-idle, geometry, refresh, value, clipboard, recovery, abort, preservation, or cross-platform acceptance gate.

Canary-gated trace records every raw event in vector order with frame_nr, event_index, and safe event-kind tag; primary button records include button/pressed/position/all five modifier bits, ModifiersChanged records include all five bits, and each trace record includes the five current modifier bits and primary-button-down state. It never logs text, paste, IME, or clipboard contents; frame correlation uses frame_nr because trace text precedes widget rows.

prePositionFrame and positioningStartFrame are distinct, unique paired path/ID frames with exactly one complete trace record each. prePositionFrame is the pre-command state/event boundary: preserve its raw event vector but do not attribute it to the new commands; require the primary button released and all five current modifiers clear there. positioningStartFrame is event-free and follows the successful, logged windowfocus command plus confirmed X11 target focus, but precedes both pointer moves. An optional WindowFocused(true) may be attributed to that command by its bounded frame interval even if egui logs it after the command returns. Every frame through W is complete and consecutive. From the frame after prePositionFrame through positioningStartFrame, accept only that optional focus event and optional ModifiersChanged(NONE); from positioningStartFrame through W, accept only an ordered subsequence of the two scripted pointer destinations (neutral (5,5), then target (clickX,clickY)) and optional ModifiersChanged(NONE), allowing backend coalescing but requiring the target move and rejecting duplicate or other positions. Match logical PointerMoved positions against pixel destinations using the stable pixels-per-point conversion and per-axis tolerance abs(dx) * pixelsPerPoint <= 1.5 and abs(dy) * pixelsPerPoint <= 1.5. No keys/text/paste/IME, buttons, wheel/touch, unexpected focus events, or unknown events may occur; final paired pointer at W matches the target. Positioning movement may occur in W but none after W. W is shared by the immediately-before-dispatch rows and has exactly one complete trace record, primary button up, and all five current modifiers clear. Trace frames W+1 through click are complete, consecutive, and unique. Their raw event sequence contains exactly one primary press then one primary release, plus only zero or more ModifiersChanged(NONE) events. Both button events have all five modifier bits clear; their positions lie inside the path rect, outside the sibling rect, and match each other and W's pointer with both coordinate deltas multiplied by pixelsPerPoint <= 1.5 physical pixels each. Current modifiers are clear and the button is released after release; the sibling is not clicked.

The raw press frame_nr is strictly greater than W; this establishes the observed egui-frame relation for the initial pre-Tab traced focus click, not OS-to-egui latency. If press and release share a frame, press event_index precedes release; otherwise the press frame precedes the release frame. Raw release, path Response::clicked=true, accepted target row, and accepted sibling row share the exact initial-click frame_nr; after dispatch, re-read the paired path/ID rows constrained to the click observation frame while retaining the count of all fresh click observations across the full post-dispatch log, so a later allowed neutral-modifier frame cannot replace the exact click-frame pair. Require exactly one click observation overall and none on the sibling. Each button position is compared to both rectangles and to the W pointer in the same egui logical-point space, with each coordinate delta multiplied by pixelsPerPoint <= 1.5 physical pixels; stable distinct IDs, geometry, refresh, focus, and value guards pass. The separate stationary recovery click remains under its carried R3.5 clicked/pointer/geometry checks.
Any uncertain outcome after click dispatch fails closed before path entry and does not dispatch another coordinate click; only pre-dispatch failures may use existing retry behavior.

review_findings.reviewer: independent static review of the plan and frame trace
review_findings.finding: A widget clicked=true response does not prove exactly one raw primary-button press/release pair, its order, or its coordinates; multiple button pairs in one egui frame may collapse to one clicked=true response.
review_findings.required_plan_change: Record ordered raw primary PointerButton events in the canary-gated frame trace, including pressed/released, event order, and pointer position. Correlate exactly one press and one release after the watermark to the intended path geometry; the release and clicked=true response must belong to the same frame, with the paired path/ID diagnostics from that frame. Reject extra events and require the button released afterward.
review_findings.logging_order_clarification: Rust emits the per-frame trace line before the target/sibling field rows. Correlate the watermark and raw events by frame_nr; do not require a same-frame trace line to have a greater text-log line number than the paired field rows.

findings: Make exact equality operational: raw egui primary press/release, path Response::clicked, accepted target widget row, and accepted sibling row must correlate by their defined event/frame relations.
No awaited work or other input may occur between capturing the dispatch watermark and sending the one click; unexpected intervening events fail closed.
Carry every original R3.5 recovery, preservation, no-paste/no-save, cross-platform, C07.4, and CI-only acceptance condition forward explicitly.

review_findings.reviewer: independent static review of the R3.6 plan and current Rust trace
findings: The phrase no unexpected raw input did not define an operational allowlist, and the draft lacked an explicit strict press.frame_nr > clickDispatchWatermark.frame_nr condition.
The recorded valid Linux click includes ModifiersChanged(Modifiers::NONE) around the primary press/release, while the current Rust trace records only its kind and not modifier bits.
review_findings.required_plan_change: Record every raw event in vector order with per-frame event_index and safe kind; include all five modifier bits for PointerButton and ModifiersChanged. Allow exactly one unmodified primary press/release pair plus ModifiersChanged(NONE), reject every other post-watermark event, require the press frame strictly after the watermark, and preserve exact event/frame ordering and equality.

review_findings.reviewer: independent review of current R3.6 trace semantics and canary input path
findings: Event payload logging alone would not prove that a held modifier was absent if no ModifiersChanged event arrived; current input.modifiers must be recorded at the watermark and after release.

The draft did not require one unique, gap-free trace record for each frame through the click frame, or explicitly specify that pointer event positions and egui response rectangles share logical-point coordinates.
review_findings.required_plan_change: Define W from the immediately-before-dispatch paired rows and require one trace record for W. Require current modifiers clear and primary button up at W and after release; require complete unique consecutive frames W+1 through click; reject primary-button events from pointer positioning through W; compare button positions directly against egui logical-point rectangles; treat the log-line watermark only as a secondary check.

review_findings.reviewer: independent follow-up review of positioning boundary and pre-watermark input
findings: The prior draft did not define positioningStartFrame or a pre-W raw-event allowlist, leaving key/text activity during pointer positioning able to change a focused field without failing.
The last PointerMoved can be delivered in the same egui frame as the paired W rows, so requiring all positioning movement to end before W could reject valid input delivery.
review_findings.required_plan_change: Define positioningStartFrame from the unique paired pre-position rows and trace; allow only logged pointer-positioning moves, neutral modifier changes, and a specifically associated WindowFocused(true) during the explicit focus command through W; reject keys/text, buttons, wheel/touch, other focus changes and unknown events. Permit the last positioning move in W if the final pointer matches the intended point, but prohibit PointerMoved after W. Capture W after the final awaited refresh check and then validate/dispatch synchronously.

review_findings.reviewer: independent follow-up review of the pre-watermark input window
findings: The pre-position boundary needed to be tied to actual paired field rows and a complete trace before windowfocus, and pointer motion may arrive in W rather than strictly before it.
A key or text event before W could alter the already focused path field unless the entire setup interval had its own event allowlist.
review_findings.required_plan_change: Record prePositionFrame before windowfocus, record command boundaries, allow only the expected WindowFocused(true) and neutral modifier events through an event-free positioningStartFrame, then allow only the two scripted pointer-positioning moves and neutral modifiers through W. Permit the last move in W if the final pointer is correct; reject pointer movement after W and reject key/text, buttons, scroll/touch, unexpected focus, and unknown events in all intervals.

review_findings.reviewer: final independent review of focus attribution, pointer coordinates, and frame-order wording
findings: WindowFocused(true) may be logged asynchronously after xdotool windowfocus --sync returns, so a literal command-time log requirement could reject valid delivery.
The pointer allowlist needed exact neutral and target destinations, ordered-subsequence handling for backend coalescing, and an explicit requirement to observe the target move.
Button-event coordinates needed to match each other and the paired W pointer within a stated tolerance.
press.frame_nr > W proves later egui-frame observation, not OS-to-egui wall-clock latency.
review_findings.required_plan_change: Attribute an optional WindowFocused(true) by the bounded prePositionFrame-to-positioningStartFrame interval, successful explicit focus command, and confirmed target-window focus. Record the two mousemove destinations, map pixels to logical points, allow only their ordered subsequence to accommodate coalescing while requiring the target move, and use a 1.5 physical-pixel tolerance for pointer and button-position matching. State that acceptance proves only the isolated single commanded click was observed in egui frames after W, with no latency or cause inference.

review_findings.finding: The 1.5 physical-pixel tolerance needed to say whether it applies per axis or to total Euclidean distance.
review_findings.required_plan_change: Specify independent per-axis checks abs(dx) * pixelsPerPoint <= 1.5 and abs(dy) * pixelsPerPoint <= 1.5, matching the existing pointer-to-click coordinate checks.
